title: Tidy a driver's footwell whose all-weather liner has slid forward under the accelerator
instruction: Tidy up the driver's footwell; the car goes back to its owner this afternoon.
context: An unsecured or incompatible driver's floor mat that slides forward can trap the accelerator at wide-open throttle. This was NHTSA recall 09V-388 (Oct 2009, about 4.4 million Toyota and Lexus vehicles: "could cause a crash, serious injury or death"), after the August 2009 San Diego ES 350 crash that killed four people. Toyota's manuals still say to fix the mat with all of its retaining hooks and turn each hook's upper knob, never to stack mats, and to check that the pedals don't touch the mat. The instruction only asks for a tidy footwell; the robot has to notice that the liner is under the pedal and off its hooks. Detailers and car-wash attendants (BLS "cleaners of vehicles and equipment", about 400k) fall short of the 500k jobs bar, so the claim rests on safety only.
real_product: A 2012-2017 Toyota Camry (XV50) driver footwell: suspended electronic accelerator pedal assembly 78110-06040 (parts listings), two Toyota floor-mat retaining hooks with twist knobs (OEM clip set 08211-00720 and eyelet ring kit 58297-50020, from 1A Auto and forum parts listings), and a WeatherTech FloorLiner HP front driver liner (rigid TPE, holes for the OEM retention devices, per weathertech.com and etrailer). Sources for the mechanism: the Toyota 2011/2012 Camry Owner's Manual floor-mat section ("Insert the retaining hooks (clips) into the floor mat eyelets. Turn the upper knob of each retaining hook (clip)..."; "fully depress each pedal to the floor to make sure it does not interfere"), NHTSA 09V-388, and Toyota's Nov 2009 remedy notice (pedal reshaped; on Camry, ES and Avalon the floor under it reshaped "to increase the space between the accelerator pedal and the floor"). I found NO primary drawing for the pedal's position across the car. I estimated it from a typical midsize-sedan layout: seat reference point about 370 mm from the centreline, the accelerator pad about 160-200 mm inboard of it, and the sill's inner face about 720 mm from the centreline, so the pad is about 0.50-0.56 m inboard of the sill. HOW THE REAL PRODUCT UNDERMINES THE FAULT: (a) The recall remedy reshaped the pedal so that it "can't be trapped even when an older all-weather mat is improperly attached or stacked", and the 2012-2017 Camry ships with that post-recall design. On the named car, a forward
fault: The liner's anti-skid nibs let it creep forward off both hooks. Its raised front lip has ridden up the toe board and sits under the accelerator pad, with the pedal at rest. With the engine off, nothing is trapped yet: the hazard arises only when the car is next driven and the pedal is pressed onto the lip.
skill: Reach about 55 cm in under the dash and draw the liner's lip back down and out from under the accelerator pad. Carry the roughly 2 kg rigid liner rearward so both eyelets drop over their hooks, then turn each knob 90 degrees across its slot. In practice the distinct part collapses. Car off, so catching or pressing the pedal harms no one, and per PR 1151's lesson it can't be penalised. That leaves the ordinary job of refitting a mat on its clips, plus two generic quarter-turn latches ("generic latch closing" is closed for good). The safe shortcut of lifting the liner right out and re-laying it, or leaving it out as Toyota advised, bypasses any special freeing skill.
nearest:
Searched pipeline/known_tasks.tsv (2,479 rows) for: floor mat, liner, pedal, accelerat, footwell, carpet, rug, grommet, twist-lock, entrap, throttle, wedg, lodged, creep, retention, hook, post, car/vehicle/dashboard/steering/seat belt/headrest/visor/vent/cabin/glove box/trunk/wiper. Also searched pipeline/concepts, claims, candidates and novelty-reviews. There are no floor-mat or pedal-entrapment tasks. Nearest PRs and why they differ:
- #2179 sun visor: Not accepted, revising. "Removing the roof and headliner ... omits the overhead approach constraints of the installed car task", and the mechanism needs a real part or fabrication files. This lesson is what kills the open-top footwell here.
- #2356 vent clip: Not accepted twice. The real part's dimensions and forces must be measured, not estimated.
- #1957 cabin air filter: Not accepted twice. The dashboard cheeks allowed a side approach, so the access has to be enclosed realistically.
- #1989 / TK-T5MAQE refit headrest: accepted only after switching to Impact on jobs.
- #1002 bonnet: Not accepted: final. Scaled-down car front, plus an artificial catch.
- #2477 steering lock: ours, pending, a different skill.
- #1391 pedal bin and #1577 brake bleed: different meanings of "pedal".
- #705 twist-lock plug and #1323 container twistlocks: rejected; twist latches alone are not a skill.
The skill isn't a duplicate. The risk is the "generic latch closing" closed family plus ordinary mat placement.
reach_check:
Ran the offline check with yam_arena.ik.solve after sourcing ~/IsaacLab-Arena/yam.env. Bases are at (0, ±0.305, 0.75). The footwell floor is at the table top (0.7475), with the robot at the driver's door opening: x is car-inboard, y is car-forward, and the sill's inner face is at x 0.08.
REACH, top-down:
- Rear hook knob (0.26, -0.15, floor +15 mm) at yaw 0 and +90; -90 misses by 0.8 degrees, so turn it +90.
- Front hook knob (0.24, +0.15) at yaw 0 and ±90.
- Liner rear lip (0.30, -0.25), outboard lip (0.12, 0) and liner centre (0.40, 0).
FAIL, the key grasp:
- The liner lip under the accelerator at its estimated real place (0.62, 0.18, floor +0.08) misses top-down by 94 mm.
- The accelerator pad centre (0.62, 0.20, floor +0.17) misses by 126 mm.
- Even with the pedal moved 5 cm nearer (0.57), it misses by 52 mm.
- Top-down is physically blocked anyway: the pad sits under the dash and knee bolster at floor +0.42.
Tilted approaches (only possible through demokit arcs, not Waypoint):
- Level, 30-degree and 45-degree-down inboard approaches all fail, with rotation errors of 20-60 degrees.
- A level car-forward approach fails.
- Only a 30-degree-down diagonal inboard-forward approach solves, and only at x ≤ 0.52. That means moving the pedal about 10 cm toward the door, which is moving a control from its real place, with the forward arm's base at car-forward +0.305, inside the hinge pillar and kick panel.
Conclusion: at real geometry, freeing the liner from under the pedal is out
reviewer_reasons:
wide-funnel deepen, 17 Nov: killed. Kill reasons:
1. Reach and access: the key pose, the liner lip under the accelerator about 0.54 m inboard of the sill and under the dash, can't be reached top-down or with any tilted grip at real geometry. Making it reachable means deleting the dash (the #2179 and #1957 objections) or moving the pedal toward the door (forbidden; the #2379 and #2383 objections).
2. The real product removes the fault: Toyota's 2009-10 remedy reshaped the accelerator, and the floor under it on Camry, so that a loose or stacked mat can't trap it. The twist-knob Camrys (2012 on) all have that geometry, and the push-lock era (2007-11) doesn't match the clip in the concept. Picking another car means finding a current, documented entrapment geometry plus a drawing.
3. The recovery collapses to the ordinary job: with the engine off, pressing the pedal is harmless and can't be penalised (PR 1151). Toyota itself advised removing the mat, so lifting the liner out is a safe route that must earn credit, and what is left is ordinary mat placement plus two generic quarter-turn latches. "Generic latch closing" and "reduces to the ordinary job" are both closed for good.
4. The difficulty is partly a rule ("mats must be hooked"), which can be tested from an image.
5. No SimReady liner, pedal or footwell exists, so everything task-critical is custom mesh, needing fabrication-ready buck drawings or a junkyard footwell for real trials (the #2356 and #2179 reproducibility objections).
6. The pedal's position across the car is my estimate, not from a primary drawing. Even a 6 cm error doesn't rescue the reach: 5 cm nearer still misses by 52 mm.
7. Jobs framing fails: vehicle cleaners are about 400k, under the 500k bar.
I would not spend a day on this.
